body.name: Finite-sample honest coordinate-rectangle endpoint rule
body.construction:
For \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(v\in\{0,1\}\), and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set
\[
 W_{i,v,j}=8m\mathbf 1\{V_i=v,J_i=j,S_i=0,T_i=v\}R_i,
 \qquad
 \overline W_{v,j}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}W_{i,v,j},
\]
\[
 \widetilde h_{v,j}=\Pi_{[-a_m,a_m]}(\overline W_{v,j}),
 \qquad
 r_{n,m}=m\sqrt{\frac{128\log(4m/\delta_0)}{n}},
\]
and
\[
 I_{v,j}=[\max\{-a_m,\widetilde h_{v,j}-r_{n,m}\},\ \min\{a_m,\widetilde h_{v,j}+r_{n,m}\}].
\]
Define the exact image of the product rectangle under the average absolute-value map by
\[
 D_v=
 \left[
  \frac1m\sum_{j=1}^{m}\min_{x\in I_{v,j}}|x|,
  \frac1m\sum_{j=1}^{m}\max_{x\in I_{v,j}}|x|
 \right].
\]
The coordinate-rectangle endpoint rule is
\[
 C^{\mathrm{rect}}_{n,m}=(-b+kD_0,\ b-kD_1),
\]
where affine operations on an interval denote its exact set image.
